move: rainbow band gradient and wordmark twist in a pixel swirl that breathes
how: A 480x270 offscreen canvas draws a rotating five-colour band gradient (one full turn per loop) with the word SWIRL punched in dark; every frame a per-pixel loop remaps that buffer through a swirl whose angle grows toward a centre that drifts on a small Lissajous, with strength 4.5*sin(2*pi*t/D) so it twists one way, unwinds, twists the other way and is zero at both ends. The result is upscaled to 1280x720 through ctx.filter blur that breathes 6 to 16px with the swirl, then saturate/contrast via CSS. A small caption sits at the bottom.
adapt: Change the gradient stops, the word drawn in drawContent, the swirl radius R and strength; keep strength on sin(2*pi*u) and the full gradient turn so the loop closes.
port: mount(el, shot) creates the output canvas and caption in el; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one {u:0->1, duration:D, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate runs the seek paint. Canvas sizes are fixed constants; the source font must be loaded before drawing text.
caveats: a JavaScript per-pixel loop over 129,600 pixels plus getImageData every frame is CPU heavy
catalog lists 22s but the file renders D=10
canvas text uses the Sharp Grotesk font, which must be loaded
